title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged Rényi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.
summary: This paper provides an exact, closed-form holographic description of a strongly coupled superfluid using the Abelian Higgs model in AdS5 at the Bogomolny point. It calculates key properties across different physical regimes, including the superfluid fraction, large-charge scaling dimensions, and Rényi entropies. This work advances the understanding of strongly correlated quantum matter using the AdS/CFT correspondence.
main_problem: To find an exact, closed-form description of the condensed phase of a strongly coupled superfluid modeled by the Abelian Higgs model in AdS5, particularly at the Bogomolny point.
main_result: The superfluid exhibits exact adherence to the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law on the planar black brane, and closed-form results are derived for the scaling dimension of large-charge states and charged Rényi entropies.
method: The analysis uses holographic duality (AdS/CFT) by studying the Abelian Higgs model in the probe limit on various backgrounds (planar, global, hyperbolic slicings).
model_or_system: The system is the Abelian Higgs model in AdS5, serving as a holographic model for a strongly coupled superfluid. The analysis focuses on the Bogomolny point where the scalar mass saturates the BF bound.
key_observables: Superfluid fraction ($n_s/n$), sound speed, attenuation, scaling dimension $\Delta(Q)$, and charged Rényi entropies.
important_parameters: Bogomolny coupling, temperature ($T$), charge ($Q$), and the probe limit ($\kappa_5/(eL) \ll 1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the probe limit, and the closed-form results are derived specifically at the Bogomolny coupling point.
paper_structure: The paper is structured by analyzing the superfluid behavior on different geometric slicings: the planar black brane (thermal superfluid), global AdS5 (large charge), and hyperbolic slicing (Rényi entropies).
why_interesting: The holographic description of superfluidity and its connection to entanglement entropy provides powerful, non-perturbative tools to study strongly correlated quantum matter, analogous to phenomena in ultracold atomic gases or high-Tc superconductors.
